text: Guido Fanti (27 May 1925 – 11 February 2012) was an Italian politician who belonged to the Italian Communist Party. Born in 1925, he attended university but was forced to leave during the Second World War. In 1943, he was called to arms but soon joined the partisan resistance. After the liberation of Bologna in 1945, he joined the Italian Communist Party. Fifteen years later, he became provincial secretary of the PCI. In 1960, he entered the central committee of the party, where he was reconfirmed in the subsequent two congresses, and in 1965, at the XI congress, he became a member of the national directorate. Fanti was elected city councilor of Bologna in 1957; on 2 April 1966, he was elected mayor of the city following Giuseppe Dozza's resignation due to health reasons, after Dozza had led the city's reconstruction and initiated economic and social recovery. During his tenure, the PEEP public housing plan and the construction of the "Fiera District" (based on a project by architect Kenzō Tange) were approved. On 29 July 1970, Fanti resigned as mayor to become the first president of the Emilia-Romagna Region. He later renounced his regional position because he was a member of the Chamber of Deputies from 1976 to 1983. In 1983, he was elected senator of the IX legislature and served until 1987. From 1979 to 1989, he served as a Member of the European Parliament (MEP), and in 1984, he became vice president of the European Parliament. Guido Fanti died in the night between 10 and 11 February 2012.
